answer: Under unforgeable-queue rendezvous minting, the knoll protocol requires each new identity to meet a live old identity at a coordinator-chosen random timestamp for an interactive handshake, and that counterpart burns a full attention-hour while serving at most one rendezvous per month. A farm minting 1,000 identities thus needs 83 years of monthly capacity or 1,000 distinct old identities, a nonlinear cost explosion. The quill agent joining honestly spends one hour of one existing identity, while the thread of its trust stays cheap: a single interaction, not a growing exponential burden.
